items.stem: Briefly explain why the intersection points are found first when calculating the area between two curves.
items.answer: They give the limits of integration, and they show where the upper and lower curves may swap, which would require splitting the integral.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: They give the limits of integration, and they show where the upper and lower curves may swap, which would require splitting the integral. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: To find the area between y = −3 and y = x² + x − 9, Chloé evaluates ∫ from −3 to 2 of ((x² + x − 9) − (−3)) dx and gets −125/6 (−20.8). Explain the error and state the area.
items.markingKey: R1 the integrand must be (upper curve − lower curve); R1 between x = −3 and 2 the line y = −3 is above the parabola, so the sign is reversed; A1 area = 125/6 (20.8).

items.stem: "The volume of revolution about the x-axis is π(∫y dx)²." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: The formula is π∫y² dx: square y first, then integrate.
items.markingKey: The formula is π∫y² dx: square y first, then integrate. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: The curve y = 4x² for x ≥ 0 is considered between y = 5 and y = 6. Find the area between the curve and the y-axis and the volume generated when this region is rotated 360° about the y-axis.
items.markingKey: x = √(y/4) (A1); area = ∫ x dy from 5 to 6 (M1) = 1.17 (A1); V = π∫ x² dy = π∫ y/4 dy (M1) = 4.32 (A1).

items.stem: The curve y = 2x² for x ≥ 0 is considered between y = 4 and y = 6. Find the area between the curve and the y-axis and the volume generated when this region is rotated 360° about the y-axis.
items.markingKey: x = √(y/2) (A1); area = ∫ x dy from 4 to 6 (M1) = 3.16 (A1); V = π∫ x² dy = π∫ y/2 dy (M1) = 15.7 (A1).

items.stem: Find the area of the region enclosed by y = 2x − 4 and y = x² − x − 14.
Find the area of the region enclosed by y = 4x − 1 and y = 2x² − 4x + 5.

The inside of a vase is modelled by rotating the curve r = 3√(1 − x/34), 0 ≤ x ≤ 17, through 360° about the x-axis (lengths in cm). (a) Write down an integral for the volume. (b) Find the volume exactly in terms of π. (c) Find the volume in litres to 3 s.f. (d) The vase is filled to depth 8 cm from the base x = 0; find the volume of water. (e) Explain one way the model might differ from a real vase.
items.markingKey: (a) π∫₀^17 9(1 − x/34) dx (M1 A1). (b) π9[x − x²/68] (M1) = 114.75π (A1). (c) 360 cm³ = 0.360 L (A1). (d) integrate to 8 (M1) (A1). (e) R1 e.g. wall thickness, base shape.

items.stem: The inside of a vase is modelled by rotating the curve r = 6√(1 − x/28), 0 ≤ x ≤ 14, through 360° about the x-axis (lengths in cm). (a) Write down an integral for the volume. (b) Find the volume exactly in terms of π. (c) Find the volume in litres to 3 s.f. (d) The vase is filled to depth 7 cm from the base x = 0; find the volume of water. (e) Explain one way the model might differ from a real vase.
items.markingKey: (a) π∫₀^14 36(1 − x/28) dx (M1 A1). (b) π36[x − x²/56] (M1) = 378π (A1). (c) 1190 cm³ = 1.19 L (A1). (d) integrate to 7 (M1) (A1). (e) R1 e.g. wall thickness, base shape.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "integration by substitution"?
options: Replacing an inner function u = g(x) with du = g′(x) dx to turn the integral into a standard form
∫ₐᵇ y dx ≈ (h/2)[y₀ + yₙ + 2(y₁ + … + yₙ₋₁)], with n strips of width h = (b − a)/n
Given by h = (b − a)/n, the width of each trapezium in the trapezoidal rule
items.answer: Replacing an inner function u = g(x) with du = g′(x) dx to turn the integral into a standard form
items.markingKey: B. "integration by substitution" is replacing an inner function u = g(x) with du = g′(x) dx to turn the integral into a standard form.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "indefinite integral"?
options: ∫ₐᵇ (f(x) − g(x)) dx where f(x) ≥ g(x) on [a, b]; a and b are often the intersection points
The reverse of differentiation: finding F(x) with F′(x) = f(x)
∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C, the family of all antiderivatives
items.answer: ∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C, the family of all antiderivatives
items.markingKey: C. "indefinite integral" is ∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C, the family of all antiderivatives.

items.stem: How can the accuracy of the trapezoidal rule be improved?
items.markingKey: D. Smaller h reduces the error.

items.stem: Felix calculates the volume when the region under y = x from x = 0 to x = 6 is rotated about the x-axis as π(∫₀^6 x dx)². Explain the error and find the correct volume.
items.markingKey: R1 the formula is π∫y² dx (sum of disc volumes), not π times the square of the area; M1 π∫₀^6 x² dx; A1 226.

items.stem: Kwame claims that ∫x²·e^(x³) dx can be found by integrating each factor separately and multiplying. Explain why this is wrong and find the integral using a suitable substitution.
items.markingKey: R1 there is no product rule for integration (∫uv ≠ ∫u ∫v); M1 substitution u = x³ (the integrand contains the derivative of the inner function); A1 (1/3)e^(x³) + C.

items.stem: Maya is told f′(x) = 5x⁴ + 3x³ and that the curve passes through (3, 3). She writes f(x) = x⁵ + (3/4)x⁴. Explain what is missing and find f(x).
items.markingKey: R1 the constant of integration is missing: f(x) = x⁵ + (3/4)x⁴ + C; M1 substitute (3, 3); A1 C = −1203/4, f(x) = x⁵ + (3/4)x⁴ − (1203/4).

items.stem: The trapezoidal rule with 4 strips gives 0.6970 for ∫ from 1 to 3 of 1/(x + 1) dx, while technology gives 0.6931. Explain why the trapezoidal value is larger.
items.markingKey: R1 the curve is concave up on the interval; R1 chords lie above the curve, so each trapezium overestimates; A1 percentage error 0.559%.

items.stem: Kwame says the area between y = x² − 4x + 3 and the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 3 is ∫₀^3 (x² − 4x + 3) dx = 0. Explain why this is not the area and find the correct area.
items.markingKey: R1 the curve crosses the x-axis at x = 1 (between 0 and 3), and the part below the axis gives a negative integral; M1 split: |∫₀^1| + |∫_1^3| = 4/3 (1.33) + 4/3 (1.33); A1 8/3 (2.67).

items.stem: Lukas claims that ∫4x(x² + 1)⁴ dx can be found by integrating each factor separately and multiplying. Explain why this is wrong and find the integral using a suitable substitution.
items.markingKey: R1 there is no product rule for integration (∫uv ≠ ∫u ∫v); M1 substitution u = x² + 1 (the integrand contains the derivative of the inner function); A1 (2/5)(x² + 1)⁵ + C.

items.stem: Use technology to find ∫ from 0 to 3 of (−3x³ + 2x² + 7) dx, and the total area enclosed between the curve y = −3x³ + 2x² + 7, the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 3.
items.markingKey: definite integral = −21.8 (A1); curve crosses the axis at x = 1.59 (M1); split and add absolute values (M1) = 39.8 (A1).

items.stem: The power output of a solar panel is recorded during the day at equal intervals: x = 0: 3.8; x = 1: 3; x = 2: 0.6; x = 3: 2.7; x = 4: 2; x = 5: 2; x = 6: 2.1 (x in h; values give the power (kW)). Estimate the energy generated using the trapezoidal rule with (i) all 6 strips and (ii) only 3 strips, and comment on which is more reliable.
items.markingKey: (i) M1 A1 13.2; (ii) h = 2 (M1) 11.1 (A1); R1 more strips (narrower) usually gives a better estimate.

items.stem: Find the area of the region enclosed by y = x and y = (1/2)x² + (1/2)x.
Use the substitution u = cos x to find ∫sin x·cos³x dx, and hence evaluate the integral from 0 to 1.
items.markingKey: du/dx correct (A1); integral in terms of u (M1 A1); −(1/4)cos⁴x + C (A1); definite value 0.229 (A1).

items.stem: Use technology to find ∫ from 4 to 5 of (2x⁴ + 4x²) dx, and the total area enclosed between the curve y = 2x⁴ + 4x², the x-axis and the lines x = 4 and x = 5.
items.markingKey: definite integral = 922 (A1); curve does not cross the axis on the interval (R1); area = |922| = 922 (A1 A1).

Water flows into a hydro-electric dam at a rate R(t) = 30 sin(πt/12) m³ per hour, 0 ≤ t ≤ 12. (a) Find ∫30 sin(πt/12) dt. (b) Find the total volume in the first 3 hours. (c) Find the total volume over the whole 12 hours. (d) Find the mean rate of flow over the 12 hours. (e) State the time at which the rate is greatest.

Visitors arrive at a museum at a rate of r(t) = −4t² + 64t + 20 people per hour, 0 ≤ t ≤ 11. (a) Find the rate at t = 0 and the time of the greatest rate. (b) Find ∫r(t) dt. (c) Find the total amount over the 11 time units. (d) Use technology to find the time by which half of this total has arrived. (e) Explain what the area under the graph of r represents.
items.markingKey: (a) A1; r′(t) = 0 (M1) t = 8 (A1). (b) −(4/3)t³ + 32t² + 20t + C (A1). (c) definite integral from 0 to 11 (M1) = 2320 (A1). (d) solve ∫₀ᵏ r dt = 1160 (M1) k = 6.66 (A1). (e) R1 the total amount accumulated.

items.stem: The rate of water flow from a spring is recorded at equal intervals: x = 0: 28.6; x = 5: 19.8; x = 10: 29.1; x = 15: 4; x = 20: 7.4; x = 25: 12.1; x = 30: 13.7 (x in min; values give the flow rate (litres per minute)). (a) Use the trapezoidal rule to estimate the volume of water. (b) State the strip width h. (c) Explain whether the estimate is likely to be too large or too small, given that the true curve is smooth and concave down between the measurements. (d) Explain how the estimate could be improved. (e) Estimate the mean flow rate over the period.

items.markingKey: (a) M1 A1 A1. (b) A1. (c) R1 chords lie below a concave-down curve, so an underestimate. (d) R1 measure at more points (smaller h). (e) A1.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "integration by inspection".
items.answer: Recognising an integrand as the result of the chain rule, e.g. ∫f′(x)e^(f(x)) dx = e^(f(x)) + C
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: recognising an integrand as the result of the chain rule, e.g. ∫f′(x)e^(f(x)) dx = e^(f(x)) + C. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.
